title: Eskenazi Health posts breach notice after phishing gave access to two employees' email accounts
date_note: The day Eskenazi Health posted its substitute notice ("Posted: November 20, 2026"); the page gives no earlier disclosure day for this incident. The notice says the unauthorized access began and was stopped on 21 September 2026. WIBC's article of 21 November gives different incident dates (see summary note in validation).
geo_basis: Eskenazi Health is Indianapolis's public hospital system (WIBC, Indianapolis local news); the notice gives no address
summary: Eskenazi Health posted a substitute breach notice saying that on 21 September 2026 an unauthorized individual gained access to two employees' cloud-based work email accounts after they followed a phishing link to a "secure" document; it ended the access that day. The emails may have held patients' contact, insurance and billing, medical and treatment information and Social Security numbers. The notice gives no number of people affected.
plain: An Indianapolis hospital system says a fake email tricked two staff members, letting someone into their work email in September. Patients' medical details and Social Security numbers may have been seen.
exec: A phishing link gave an intruder access to two hospital employees' email accounts holding patient medical, insurance and Social Security data.
action: Eskenazi Health's notice advises affected people to review their credit reports with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion and offers identity theft protection, including credit monitoring, at no cost (call 833-931-8866).
impact: Number of people affected not stated in the notice.

sources.name: Eskenazi Health: Security Incident November 2026 (substitute data breach notice)
WIBC: Eskenazi Patient Data Exposed in Breach

key_findings: On 21 September 2026 Eskenazi Health discovered an unauthorized individual had gained access to two employees' cloud-based work accounts; the access was terminated the same day.
The employees received a phishing email that appeared to come from a business partner, with a link tied to a "secure" document notification.

Information involved varied by individual: demographic and contact information, health insurance and billing information, medical record numbers, medical and treatment information, substance use disorder information and Social Security numbers.
recommendations: Review credit reports maintained by the credit reporting bureaus.
Enrol in the identity theft protection offered at no cost.

validation.note: Primary: Eskenazi Health's own substitute notice posted 20 November 2026 states the core facts (two employees, phishing, access ended 21 September). WIBC (21 November) does not describe the phishing or the two employees and gives different dates: it says access 'may have started June 3' with incidents identified on July 27, Aug. 31 and Sept. 26; the notice does not mention these and the difference is unexplained. This record follows the notice's own dates. No count of affected people on either page; no HHS breach portal entry read.

review.note: validation: removed unsupported claim about a separate October notice that was not read; WIBC conflicts on dates and lacks the phishing and two-employee facts, so state set to single_source on the primary notice; title, date, summary, action, sectors checked against the notice
